---
title: "How does performance change if we actually compute the flight path?"
---

{{< include _model.qmd >}}

```{python}
# The aircraft is chapter 01's optimum, unchanged; only the method differs.
opt = optimise(static_margin=0.10)
plane, layout = design_geometry(opt)

ANGLES = [5, 10, 20, 30, 45, 60]
flights = {a: simulate(plane, layout, ballast=opt["ballast"], launch_angle=a)
           for a in ANGLES}
best = max(flights.values(), key=lambda f: f["duration"])
stall = flights[30]
loop = flights[45]
speed_ratio = V_LAUNCH / opt["V"]
turn = float(np.max(np.abs(loop["theta"])))

assert all(f["landed"] for f in flights.values())   # none ran out of t_max
assert best["duration"] < opt["duration"]           # the trim method was optimistic
assert turn > 360                                   # it really does go right over
assert stall["alpha_max"] > 90                      # and shallow launches fly backwards
assert loop["skim_altitude"] < 0.05                 # the best flight grazes the ground
```

::: {.hero-pair}
::: {.hero-ref}

:::
::: {}
[`{python} f"{best['duration']:.1f} s"`]{.hero-value}

:::
:::

**Answer.** It loops. Thrown at
[`{python} f"{speed_ratio:.1f}"`×]{.key} its trim speed the wing makes several
times the glider's weight, so at
`{python} f"{loop['launch_angle']:.0f}"`° it goes right over the top through
[`{python} f"{turn:.0f}"`°]{.key} before settling into a glide (@fig-path).
Shallower, it runs out of airspeed at the apex, flips backwards through
`{python} f"{stall['alpha_max']:.0f}"`° and lands
`{python} f"{stall['range']:.1f}"` m away.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Two reasons to read this as a ceiling
It grazes `{python} f"{loop['skim_altitude']*1e3:.0f}"` mm at
`{python} f"{loop['skim_t']:.1f}"` s — over grass it lands there, not at
`{python} f"{best['duration']:.1f}"` s. And no section model is fitted near
`{python} f"{stall['alpha_max']:.0f}"`°.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}

```{python}
#| label: fig-path
#| fig-cap: "Flight path, side on, for the best launch and a shallow one, with markers every half second. Dashed line is the ground, star is the release point."
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.0, 3.0))
for f, lab, c in [(loop, f"{loop['launch_angle']:.0f}° — loops, then glides", "C0"),
                  (stall, f"{stall['launch_angle']:.0f}° — stalls at the apex", "C3")]:
    ax.plot(f["x"], f["altitude"], color=c,
            label=f"{lab}  ({f['duration']:.1f} s)")
    m = np.arange(0, len(f["t"]), max(1, int(0.5 / (f["t"][1] - f["t"][0]))))
    ax.plot(f["x"][m], f["altitude"][m], "o", color=c, ms=3)
ax.axhline(0, ls="--", lw=1, color="C2")
ax.plot(0, H_RELEASE, "k*", ms=10, label="release")
ax.set_xlabel("horizontal distance, m")
ax.set_ylabel("altitude, m")
ax.set_ylim(-0.2, None)
ax.grid()
ax.legend(loc="upper left", fontsize=7)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
